doc.title: tTJSVariant Type
doc.para: What is tTJSVariant The tTJSVariant type is a type that handles "variable" data in TJS2. The tTJSVariant type has an internal type, and a single type can represent void (undefined), object, integer, real number, string, and octet sequence. In addition, it automatically handles conversions between these internal types during operations.

tTJSVariantType This is an enumeration type representing the internal type of tTJSVariant. It can be obtained using the tTJSVariant::Type method.
tvtVoid
It is the void type. When constructing a tTJSVariant type with a parameterless constructor, it becomes this type. It is not null.
tvtObject
It is the object type. In the case of null, it becomes this internal type.
tvtString
It is the string type.
tvtOctet
It is the octet sequence type.
tvtInteger
It is the integer type. It holds numerical values of the tTVInteger type.
tvtReal
It is the real number type. It holds numerical values of the tTVReal type.

Object Reference Among internal types, objects are managed using the reference counting method. Although tTJSVariant itself automatically manages the reference count, please note that it does not manage the reference count after extracting an object pointer via methods that retrieve or methods that retrieve the tTJSVariantClosure type from tTJSVariant.

Object Type The tTJSVariantClosure type is a type that holds an object inside tTJSVariant. This type has a mechanism to hold two iTJSDispatch2 interfaces: one holds the object itself, and the other holds information about the context in which that object is executed. The tTJSVariantClosure type has each of the methods possessed by the iTJSDispatch2 interface. By accessing these methods via tTJSVariantClosure, you can correctly process the execution context.
To extract the tTJSVariantClosure type from the tTJSVariant type, there are two methods: tTJSVariant::AsObjectClosure and tTJSVariant::AsObjectClosureNoAddRef. The former increments the object's reference counter, while the latter does not. Since the tTJSVariantClosure type does not have a mechanism to automatically manage reference counts, you need to be careful with reference count management after extracting the tTJSVariantClosure type from a tTJSVariant type.

String Type Strings in TJS2 are managed using the reference counting method; simple operations like copying only increase the string's reference counter, and the string body itself is not duplicated. The tTJSVariantString type is a type used in the tTJSVariant type and tTJSString type to manage strings. To extract the tTJSVariantString type from a tTJSVariant type, you can use tTJSVariant::AsString (this method increments the reference counter). However, because the tTJSVariantString type itself does not have a mechanism to automatically manage reference counts, caution is required when using tTJSVariantString. Since the tTJSString type can manage the reference counter, it is easier to convert to the tTJSString type (conversion operators between tTJSVariant and tTJSString are defined).

Octet Sequence Type Like string types, octet sequences in TJS2 are managed using the reference counting method. The tTJSVariantOctet type is a type for managing octet sequences. Please note that, like tTJSVariantString and tTJSVariantClosure, this type does not have a mechanism to manage reference counts. To extract the tTJSVariantOctet type from the tTJSVariant type, you can use tTJSVariant::AsOctet (increments the reference counter) or tTJSVariant::AsOctetNoAddRef (does not increment the reference counter).

Conversion Since various conversion operators and constructors are defined for tTJSVariant, it can be handled like a primitive type. As mentioned above, care must be taken when performing conversions with types managed by reference counters.
Operations Since various operators are overloaded, operations can also be performed just like primitive types. Type conversions required during the operation process are automatically handled.
